DRAFT PREDECISIONAL
All:
We will have a meeting with Meta (aiming the last week of September) to reset on ways that Meta and Whatsapp can support USAID
missions and partners. We plan to discuss support and engagement that loosely ties to these three categories:
Categories:
1. Resilience Building
a. Trainings on digital literacy and access to information
b. Trainings on mis/disinfo related to political processes and elections,
c. Connecting partners with digital platforms and independent fact checking organizations
d. Engagement around preventing, mitigating, and responding to technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV).
experienced by women in politics and public life on Meta's and other widely-used platforms.
e. Prevention and Response to Irregular Migration, Trafficking in Persons (TIP) and Human Smuggling
Engagement around preventing, mitigating, and responding to migrant smuggling (coyotes) and human
trafficking experienced by Guatemalans on Meta's and other widely-used platforms as a means for recruitment
and communication.
Engagement around preventing, mitigating, and responding to fraud and misinformation campaigns regarding
temporary work visa programs.
ili.Engagement around mitigating the use of Meta products in the formation of mass migrant movements
(Caravans) and cross-national migrant movements.
2. Support to our missions and partners (expedited review)
a. Strengthening relationships and fostering collaboration between mission partners/civil society and Meta; external
engagement
b. Improving the response time and overall responsiveness to partner organizations' (civil society, media et al) cases
with Meta that involve hacking, blackmailing, hate speech etc. especially in the countries of Global South.
3. Awareness and information sharing (local partners and missions ability to share on-the-ground information and experiences)
during steady state and key events.
Sincerely, Vera

Support:
Our implementing partner BBC media action
(BBCMA) is blocked by Meta from boosting their
postings to share public interest stories, election
related information and countering mis/disinformation
with their El Kul platform on Facebook. USAID and
BBCMA have failed to unlock this issue and now it is
impacting critical life saving information to the
humanitarian disaster in eastern Libya. How can we
solve this issue to boost the reach of El Kul's posts?
El Kul is a Libyan social media platform with over 1.2
million followers. A team of Libya-based freelance
reporters and Tunis-based BBC Media Action content
producers make daily El Kul content that promotes
the inclusion and participation of women in society
and tolerance of diversity amid the conflict.
BBCMA has been struggling with boosting and
promoting posts related to elections related issues
and has tried to address this issue with Meta
regionally throughout 2023 to their MENA teams.
They have also raised this issue with Vera when she
was in Tunis in May 2023. However, the issue
remains unresolved.
Following the recent massive flooding in eastern
Libya from Storm Daniel, Meta was blocking the
boosting of potential life saving information from
BBCMA. El Kul is the only Libyan communication
platform providing emergency communication on
lifesavina issues such as cleaning drinking water,
avoiding the most dangerous locations, and
effectively coordinatina and accessina assistance at
scale. El Kul was able to effectively appeal the

that affect what we do?
- Use agendas and clear talking points with GC: that way we have a paper trail of all the conversations we have in case
needed for a legal reason
- We can provide input into general principles, but let's work closely with GC on anything that touches near content moderation
- Exercise additional caution if talking to social companies about their content moderation
- See point about agenda and talking points
- Encourage direct collaboration between platforms and partners, so we are not part of the conversation
Independent reporting

- Not covered by the injunction, but in case it is, there is a carve out in the injunction for this
Concern: If partner discovers content that violates platform policy (e.g. illegal act, call for violence), by raising that to the platform,
there's an implicit suggestion of content moderation.
- Content moderation referrals are different than content moderation direction
- Make it clear that it's a referral and not something else; we don't want to cross the line into a directive
Request to have a session with GC on this with missions
Challenges/Difficulties with previous Meta engagement?
- LAC: Trainings for mission partners have not always been great. Feedback:
- Trainings were too basic for what we had requested (esp. Mis disinfo in elections)
- Others have been better
- One is being planned for mission doxx in LAC
- In general relationship has been positive and Meta has been responsive
- LAC has engaged Meta in some interagency discussions around civic space during public events
When working with Meta, have to work through existing tools they have available. They're not going to spin up a new training/invest
in a new country if it doesn't suit their bottom line. What are the things that they already offer and how can we help direct some of
those resources more strategically?
